question: An engineer must configure port aggregation between two Cisco MDS 9000 Series Switches. The solution must meet these requirements: suspend member interface if parameters mismatch; load-balance traffic on multiple ports; and support traffic from multiple VSANs. Which port channel configuration must be used?
options: Port type: FT Port - Port channel mode: Active
Port type: F Port - Port channel mode: On
Port type: E Port - Port channel mode: Active
Port type: TE Port - Port channel mode: On
theory: To aggregate multiple ISLs between two MDS switches into a single logical link that load-balances traffic, suspends a mismatched member automatically, and can carry multiple VSANs, the port type must be E port, the standard switch-to-switch FC port type capable of trunking multiple VSANs, and the channel mode must be Active so member ports run port-channel-protocol negotiation, automatically detect parameter mismatches, and suspend any port that doesn't match rather than silently forming an inconsistent channel, which On mode would allow. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 8 - SAN Port Channels)
